subject: botany
question_text: Write the differences between red algae and brown algae.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack botany section, Chapter 4 Plant Kingdom, book p.8, SAQ 1. The book's table prints 'Floridian starch' and 'laminarian'; the correct names floridean starch and laminarin are used here. Only one source book is held for botany — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand is physics-only and no botany board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card, not merely unrun. The four-row 1-mark-each split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

steps.label: Pigments
lines: Red algae: chlorophyll a, d and
Brown algae: chlorophyll a, c and
steps.why: The accessory pigment decides the colour and the class name: phycoerythrin makes Rhodophyceae red, fucoxanthin makes Phaeophyceae brown.
common_mistakes: Writing chlorophyll b for either group — b belongs to green algae; red has a and d, brown has a and c.
steps.memory_tip: Chlorophyll pairs in order: green a + b, brown a + c, red a + d — the letters b, c, d follow the three groups.
steps.margin_note: One contrast row = one mark; write both sides of every row.

steps.label: Cell wall
lines: Brown algae: cellulose with an outer
steps.why: Both walls start with cellulose; the outer layer differs — sulphate esters in red algae, the gelatinous algin coat in brown algae.
common_mistakes: Writing 'algin' for red algae — algin is the brown-algae coat.
Writing chitin — chitin belongs to fungal walls, not algae.
steps.memory_tip: Brown → algin: brown algae are the commercial source of algin, so the wall coat and the product are the same word.
steps.margin_note: Cellulose alone is not a difference — name the outer layer on each side.

steps.label: Stored food
steps.why: Each class keeps its own reserve carbohydrate. The book prints 'Floridian starch' and 'laminarian'; the correct names are floridean starch and laminarin.
common_mistakes: Spelling errors — it is floridean starch and laminarin; the book itself prints both words wrongly.
steps.memory_tip: The word 'florid' means reddish — floridean starch belongs to the red algae.
steps.margin_note: Name the reserve on both sides; the bracket detail is a safe extra.

steps.label: Sexual reproduction
steps.why: Red-algae gametes cannot swim, so reproduction is only oogamous; brown-algae gametes swim with two flagella, so all three forms occur.
common_mistakes: Writing motile gametes for red algae — non-motile gametes are their marked feature.
Listing only 'oogamy' for brown algae — they show all three forms.
steps.memory_tip: Red = one method, no swimming; brown = all three methods, swimming gametes.
steps.margin_note: Four rows earn the four marks; examples (Polysiphonia vs Laminaria) are optional extras.

insider_note: Write this as a two-column table with four rows — pigments, wall, food, reproduction; examiners award one mark per correct row.
